short: Silent-EMG-to-text without vocalized pairing and SPD inputs are both standard: subvocal-only label training predates it, and 73.53% WER from one person is tested only against a near-chance baseline.
position: The paper changes training-only supervision (M02: phoneme transcriptions of silent EMG, no vocalized recordings) and the input representation (M06: SPD covariance matrices into a GRU with CTC); both are standard. Subvocal-only phoneme models for 2,200-word continuous phrases were trained without vocalized pairing by 2018, at 8.9% mean WER over four phrase sets under a grammar, so the priority claim rests on its qualifiers (general English corpora, modern methods); the paper cites that work only as a 200-word grammar system. The SPD gain (PER 89.25% to 48.47%, WER 100% to 73.53%) is measured against a spectrogram baseline close to the 97.5% chance PER, in one participant with no repeated runs reported. The paper does not evaluate on the public silent-EMG benchmark, where text decoding with vocalized pairing reaches 12.2% WER, so the cost of dropping vocalized supervision is unmeasured.
